sentences.text: As per the F.I.R. lodged by prosecutrix, she was serving in State Bank of India on the post of Senior Associate in the year 2017.
The appellant was also posted in the same Branch as Junior Associate.
During course of their conversation, he gain the confidence of the prosecutrix and gave an impression that he likes her very much.

In 2017, it is alleged that on one occasion, he has gone to her house where she was given food and after consuming it she came in stage of intoxication and he taking advantage of it, he established physical relationship.
It is also alleged that he threatened to upload nude pictures of the prosecutrix.
It is submitted by the learned counsel on behalf of appellant that there is inordinate delay in institution of FIR by six years.
Offence under Section 376 of the IPC will not be made out as both were adults and there is no material to show that force or fraud was used.
The date and time of the incidence has also not been stated in the FIR.
Further, the allegation of threat to upload the photograph of objectionable condition on social media has also not been made out as the offence under I.T. Act has not been lodged.
It is argued that under this circumstance offence under Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 2015.

sentences.text: Learned counsel on behalf of informant has not opposed the bail application and has not denied the factual assertion made by the learned counsel on behalf of appellant and has admitted that the matter has been duly compromised.

Considering the submissions made, the appellant, above named, is directed to surrender before the learned trial court within a period of two weeks and in the event of his arrest or surrender, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only)
with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the Court below, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Criminal Appeal is allowed.
I.A. No.3944 of 2024 is disposed of.
